posts.content:
Ceci est une page d’exemple. C’est différent d’un article de blog parce qu’elle restera au même endroit et apparaîtra dans la navigation de votre site (dans la plupart des thèmes). La plupart des gens commencent par une page « À propos » qui les présente aux personnes visitant le site. Cela pourrait ressembler à quelque chose comme cela :

Bonjour ! Je suis un mécanicien qui aspire à devenir acteur, et voici mon site. J’habite à Bordeaux, j’ai un super chien baptisé Russell, et j’aime la vodka (ainsi qu’être surpris par la pluie soudaine lors de longues balades sur la plage au coucher du soleil).

…ou quelque chose comme cela :

La société 123 Machin Truc a été créée en 1971, et n’a cessé de proposer au public des machins-trucs de qualité depuis lors. Située à Saint-Remy-en-Bouzemont-Saint-Genest-et-Isson, 123 Machin Truc emploie 2 000 personnes, et fabrique toutes sortes de bidules supers pour la communauté bouzemontoise.

En tant que nouvel utilisateur ou utilisatrice de WordPress, vous devriez vous rendre sur votre tableau de bord pour supprimer cette page et créer de nouvelles pages pour votre contenu. Amusez-vous bien !

posts.title: To design Digital Strategy
posts.content:
01. A clearer digital direction

Northline Studio wanted to bring its website, social channels and editorial calendar together. The challenge was to build a consistent voice while keeping enough flexibility for product launches, customer stories and everyday updates.

We began with a detailed review of the existing customer journey. Clarity was the main priority: visitors needed to understand the offer, find relevant examples and know what to do next. We also looked at how the same message could move from a short social post to a longer landing page without losing its meaning.

02. From research to an editorial system

The strategy combines three complementary themes: practical advice, stories from the team and a closer look at the work itself. Each theme has its own rhythm, but all of them share a simple vocabulary and a recognisable visual structure.

  • Audit: review the content, navigation and main entry points.
  • Positioning: define a clear promise and a consistent tone of voice.
  • Content: prepare reusable formats for articles, campaigns and case studies.
  • Measurement: choose a small set of useful signals rather than a long list of vanity metrics.

A good digital strategy helps people make the next decision with confidence.

Northline Studio — project brief

03. A practical roadmap

  1. Start with the pages that explain the offer and answer the most common questions.
  2. Introduce a shared editorial calendar and a small library of visual templates.
  3. Review the journey regularly and adjust the content using feedback from real conversations.

The final deliverables include a content map, a campaign framework and a set of reusable templates. Together, they give the team a concrete starting point for future communication. The next step is to connect these materials with the other projects in the portfolio.

04. What the team can reuse

This project is designed around repeatable decisions. Instead of starting every campaign from a blank page, the team can choose an audience, a message and a format from a shared system. Short announcements and longer stories now follow the same logic, making it easier to keep the experience coherent across different touchpoints.

posts.title: UI Design
posts.content:
01. A compact identity refresh

Mori Studio needed a simple visual identity for a new collection. We focused on a distinctive mark, a restrained colour palette and a small set of applications that could be used immediately.

02. Small details, consistent impact

The identity works through proportion, spacing and contrast. A limited number of elements makes the system easy to recognise, whether it appears on a printed card or a small digital surface.

The result is a focused toolkit: one main mark, a compact palette and clear guidance for everyday use.

posts.title: UI Design
posts.content:
01. Making a complex workspace easier to navigate

Atelier Horizon is a demonstration of a workspace where several teams collaborate on the same projects. The interface brings together planning, project information and shared resources without asking users to switch constantly between unrelated screens.

The challenge was to handle both quick visits and longer working sessions. Someone checking a deadline should find it immediately; someone preparing a review needs more detail. We designed a hierarchy that supports both situations, with concise summaries at the top and progressive access to the supporting information.

02. Two complementary perspectives

For the project team

A clear overview highlights the next action, the current status and the person responsible. Longer descriptions remain available without making the first screen difficult to scan.

  • Find current tasks quickly.
  • Read the context before making a decision.
  • Keep shared information in one place.

For the reviewer

A dedicated review path gathers the objectives, key screens and open questions. The structure also accommodates a much longer comment, so the team can document edge cases without shortening an explanation that needs context.

03. One interface, several image formats

The following gallery combines landscape views and more compact details. It keeps the original image proportions and uses wider spacing so that each screen can be read separately. Captions provide a second level of information when a visual needs context.

04. A delivery that supports future iterations

The interface should remain understandable when the project becomes more complex, not only when the screen is almost empty.

Atelier Horizon — design principle

The handover includes the main screens, their component states and notes about content behaviour. The documentation covers short labels, longer explanations and incomplete information, giving future contributors a practical way to extend the interface without rebuilding its foundations.
